question.text: According to DPIIT guidelines, a start-up in India must not have recorded a turnover of more than:

answer.text: INR 25 crore in any financial year
INR 50 crore in any financial year
INR 100 crore in any financial year
INR 200 crore in any financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: The DPIIT start-up definition requires that the entity be not more than 10 years old and that it has not recorded a turnover of more than INR 100 crore in any financial year. The entity must also be engaged in innovation, development or improvement of products or processes, or operate a scalable business model with potential for employment generation or wealth creation. The Trap: The INR 25 crore figure is a familiar number from elsewhere in the AIF ecosystem (such as angel-fund investment thresholds) and can be confused with the DPIIT turnover ceiling, which is INR 100 crore. Note: Kept the INR 100 crore key and tightened the explanation to the source-backed DPIIT definition. Removed the unsupported claims about Section 80-IAC tax benefits and angel-tax exemption, which would need their own source before being asserted.
